summary: The one-liner adds `& finite` to the `even` rule so `even -> finite` now holds, fixing the reported case. But it only patches `even`; `odd` (defined symmetrically as `integer & !even`) is left unchanged, so `Symbol(odd=True).is_finite` is still None and the asymmetry lets an infinite integer be wrongly inferred as odd.

issues.description: Fix is asymmetric/incomplete: `odd == integer & !even` is untouched, so odd numbers still do NOT imply finite (Symbol('m', odd=True).is_finite == None). Same class of bug the issue reports, only half-fixed. Proper fix should also constrain odd (or add finite at the integer level).

Asymmetry introduces a wrong inference: for a symbol declared integer=True, finite=False, `even` becomes False (needs finite), then `odd == integer & !even` yields odd=True. So an 'infinite integer' is now incorrectly classified as odd, which was undetermined (None) before this change.

Change resolves exactly the reproduction case (even) without generalizing to the symmetric odd case, suggesting the patch is tailored to the reported example rather than the underlying 'integer should imply finite' principle.
